controls.title: Multi-factor authentication, and defining the suitable authentication factors and their numbers as well as the suitable authentication techniques based on th…

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Multi-factor authentication, and defining the suitable authentication factors and their numbers as well as the suitable authentication techniques based on the result of impact assessment of authentication failure and bypass for remote access and for privileged accounts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Remote-access services (RDP/SSH) or admin portals directly exposed to the internet; attack surface is elevated and MFA enforcement is not externally confirmable.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: External port scan: detect remote-access services --- RDP (3389), SSH (22) --- and admin/VPN login portals exposed directly to the internet rather than gated behind a VPN concentrator. Direct exposure is the externally observable signal; whether a second authentication factor is enforced is only revealed after first-factor authentication and is assessed at Tier 2.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Restrict remote access behind VPN with MFA; close direct exposure of RDP/SSH.

controls.title: Validation of the entity’s email service domains by using Sender Policy Framework (SPF), Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM), and Domain Message Authenticatio…

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Validation of the entity’s email service domains by using Sender Policy Framework (SPF), Domain Keys Identified Mail (DKIM), and Domain Message Authentication Reporting and Conformance (DMARC).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Missing or misconfigured SPF or DMARC records; DMARC policy set to none (non-enforcement); DKIM absent at all probed selectors (selector-limited, as DKIM selectors are not enumerable via DNS).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Authoritative DNS query for SPF TXT record; DNS query for DKIM records at a catalog of common selectors (selector._domainkey; e.g., default, google, selector1, selector2, k1, mail); DNS query for _dmarc TXT record; check DMARC policy (none/quarantine/reject).

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Publish SPF record covering all sending IPs; configure DKIM signing; publish DMARC at quarantine or reject policy.

controls.title: Encryption of data in-transit and at-rest, as per their classification and the relevant legislative and regulatory requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption of data in-transit and at-rest, as per their classification and the relevant legislative and regulatory requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Legacy TLS version or weak cipher suite in use; expired or invalid certificate; HSTS absent; data in transit unencrypted or weakly encrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: TLS handshake inspection on all external-facing services: detect TLS version (flag 1.0, 1.1 as deprecated); check cipher suite strength (flag RC4, DES, 3DES, MD5-based suites); verify certificate validity, expiry, and chain trust; check HSTS header presence. Note: external TLS inspection evidences data-in-transit encryption only; at-rest encryption is not externally observable and requires Tier 2 internal review.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1; enforce TLS 1.2 minimum with TLS 1.3 preferred; replace weak cipher suites; renew certificates; configure HSTS with long max-age.

controls.title: Use of web application firewall.

parts.prose: Use of web application firewall.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: No WAF signature detected on external web application; web application exposed to direct attack without application-layer filtering.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: HTTP response header fingerprinting: detect WAF presence via x-sucuri-id, cf-ray, x-waf-*, server behavior on malformed requests, and cookie patterns.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Deploy WAF in front of all external web applications; configure OWASP rule sets; verify WAF is in blocking mode.

controls.title: Adoption of the multi-tier architecture principle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Adoption of the multi-tier architecture principle.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Origin server directly reachable without reverse-proxy or CDN fronting (no fronting tier observed); internal tier separation requires Tier 2 confirmation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: HTTP/DNS analysis: detect whether the origin server is exposed directly versus fronted by a reverse proxy or CDN. Fronting presence or absence is externally observable; the application's internal tier separation is not externally observable, so full assessment of the multi-tier principle requires Tier 2 design review.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Implement reverse proxy or CDN fronting; separate application logic from public-facing layer.

controls.title: Use of secure protocols (e.g

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Use of secure protocols (e.g. HTTPS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: HTTP accessible without HTTPS redirect; HSTS absent or max-age insufficient; certificate invalid or expired.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: HTTP request on port 80: check for redirect to HTTPS; check for HSTS header (Strict-Transport-Security); check HSTS max-age (flag values below 6 months); verify certificate validity. Content-security response headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) are additionally recorded as web-hardening indicators but do not gate this secure-protocol control.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Enforce HTTPS on all endpoints; configure HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect; deploy HSTS with max-age ≥ 15 768 000 and includeSubDomains. Separately, harden content-security response headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin).

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Draft and approve a user security usage policy aligned with ECC 2-15-3-4; distribute to all users; attest distribution date and acknowledgement mechanism.

parts.prose: Protection of entity’s data by cloud and hosting service providers in accordance with its classification level and returning data (in a usable format) upon service completion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Data protection by cloud provider is contractually required.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Cloud SLA and data handling agreement reviewed via questionnaire.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Upload cloud SLA and data handling clauses.

controls.title: Separation of the entity’s environment (especially virtual servers) from environments of other entities within the cloud computing service provider.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Separation of the entity’s environment (especially virtual servers) from environments of other entities within the cloud computing service provider.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cloud environment is logically isolated from other tenants, confirmed by cloud provider documentation or configuration evidence.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Cloud environment isolation requires provider documentation or configuration evidence (e.g. VPC/VNET configuration, tenant isolation attestation, dedicated instance records) reviewed via structured questionnaire or evidence upload. Note: shared IP addresses and co-hosted TLS certificates are normal in multi-tenant cloud environments and do not indicate insufficient isolation.

parts.name: remediation
parts.prose: Obtain cloud provider documentation confirming logical isolation; configure dedicated VPC/VNET where feasible; include isolation requirements in cloud SLA.

parts.name: statement

parts.name: guidance

parts.name: assessment-method

parts.name: remediation
